To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) activity-induced expression of the synaptic plasticity protein Arc is reduced in granule cells in the hippocampus in mice expressing human amyloid precursor proteins (hAPP); (2) this reduction is not due to plaque formation, but rather to a deficit in the activity of NMDA receptor-dependent signaling pathways that are known to regulate Arc expression; (3) Arc reductions are accompanied by reductions in the actine-binding protein α-Actinin2 and the calcium-binding protein calbindin

the expression of the activity-regulated gene Arc, which is important for memory formation and maintenance, is reduced in the dentates gyrus of transgenic mice that overexpress the human amyloid precursor proteins.
activity-induced expression of Arc and α- actinin-2 is reduced in the dentates of hAPP mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Arc expression in synaptic function.
the role of activity-induced expression of the immediate early gene Arc (activity-regulated cytoskeleton-associated protein) for maintenance of long term potentiation and for learning.

the role of the immediate early gene Arc in memory consolidation and the effects of the Alzheimer's disease-related human amyloid precursor (hAPP) gene on Arc expression and other factors involved in synaptic plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of Arc is reduced in hAPP mice, and this reduction correlates with deficits in α-actinin, calbindin, and Fos.
Arc expression is reduced in the dentrate gyrus in hAPP mice, and this reduction correlates with the reduction of α-actinin 2.
the reduction of Arc expression in dentate gyrus is due to the reduction of α-actinin2 expression in dentate granule neurons in hAPP mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Arc expression and phosphorylation of NR2B, α-actinin, and ERK1-2 in the dentate granule neurons of hAPP mice were reduced, suggesting that the dentate gyruses of hAPP mice have impaired synaptic plasticity.
the expression of the immediate early gene Arc is reduced in the dentatate gyrus of transgenic mice expressing human amyloid precursor proteins and amyloid-beta peptides.
Arc and α-Actinin-2 are important for the formation of new memories, and that their levels are decreased in Alzheimer's Disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hAPP/Aβ mouse model exhibits a region-specific depletion of activity-dependent factors that are important for memory consolidation.

the dentate gyruses of transgenic mice with human amyloid precursor gene expression and amyloid beta peptide production are vulnerable to the effects of amyloid beta peptide, and that this is associated with a loss of activity-dependent expression of the immediate early gene arc, and of α-actinin2.
the dentate granule neurons are particularly vulnerable to hAPP/Aβ toxicity.
